description: DEF CON 33 Packet Hacking Village features presentations on traffic analysis, detection pipelines, and honeypot design. The sessions at this event cover deepfake media detection, IoT telemetry contextualization, bot fingerprinting with dynamic deception, and the history of interactive SSH honeypot workshops.

talks.title: Deepfake Image and Video Detection
talks.teaser: Methods and forensic techniques for identifying AI-generated, GAN-produced, and photoshopped fake images and videos.
talks.summary:
Overview of Deepfake Analysis

Performing analysis of fake images and videos can be challenging considering the plethora of techniques used to create deepfakes. This session explores methods for identifying fake images and videos whether created by AI, photoshopped, or GAN-generated media.

Detection Techniques and Tooling

A live demonstration walks through methods of exposing signs of alteration or AI generation using more than a dozen techniques to uncover forgeries. The session also highlights a free GPT tool for performing deepfake analysis, alongside resources and considerations for the future of deepfake detection.

talks.title: Hacking Context for Auto Root Cause and Attack Flow Discovery
talks.teaser: LLM-free alert contextualization and modular correlation pipeline to uncover root causes and attack flows in noisy IoT environments.
talks.summary:
Alert Noise in IoT Environments

IoT environments generate massive, noisy streams of logs and alerts, most of which lack the context required for effective detection and response. This presentation introduces an LLM-free approach to large-scale alert contextualization that operates without complex query authoring or heavy machine learning models.

Modular Correlation and Contextualization Logic

Lightweight, modular correlation logic automatically enriches logs, infers context, and groups related events across sensors, devices, and cloud services. By analyzing time, topology, and behavioral attributes, the system constructs causality sequences that explain what happened, where, and why without relying on human-crafted rules or expensive AI inference.

Practical Deployment

The approach provides practical techniques and open-source tools for deploying contextualization pipelines in resource-constrained IoT, industrial OT networks, smart home environments, and edge devices.

talks.title: Fingerprint-Based Bot Blocking & Dynamic Deception
talks.teaser: Lightweight reverse proxy and AI agent system using TLS and HTTP fingerprints to block bots and drive dynamic deception.
talks.summary:
Limitations of IP-Based Blocking

IP blocklists rapidly lose effectiveness as attackers cycle through addresses within minutes. In contrast, client TLS and HTTP fingerprints persist across extended campaigns, providing stable identifiers for traffic filtering.

Finch Reverse Proxy Architecture

Finch operates as a lightweight reverse proxy designed to evaluate incoming connections before traffic reaches production infrastructure or research honeypots. The proxy inspects connection attributes—including JA3, JA4, JA4H, and HTTP/2 parameters—to make immediate allow, block, or routing decisions.

AI Agent Dynamic Deception

A custom AI agent processes the event stream generated by Finch. The agent automatically updates filtering rules, suppresses noise from routine scanning bots, and generates synthetic stub responses for unhandled HTTP request paths. This adaptive response pipeline converts passive honeypots and proxies into dynamic deception systems.

talks.title: SSH Honeypots and Walkthrough Workshops: A History
talks.teaser: History and creative engineering of Cowrie-based SSH honeypot challenges and interactive puzzles at DEF CON Walkthrough Workshops.
talks.summary:
Origins of the Walkthrough Workshops

At DEF CON 24, an open-network SSH honeypot puzzle sparked the creation of the Packet Hacking Village Walkthrough Workshops. While the workshops eventually moved away from Cowrie, interactive honeypots shaped the design of subsequent village challenges.

Customizing Cowrie SSH Honeypots

While Cowrie operates as a medium-interaction SSH honeypot by default, custom engineering can substantially increase the level of interaction. The session reviews modifications developed over several years, including custom commands, terminal adventure games, and simulated file systems structured as spatial cubes to challenge participants.
